messages:
Kevin: RFC follow-up — proposal for a 'dynamic bit negotiation' API + per-layer degradation limits. TL;DR: keep runtime fallback deterministic and tiny, surface policy complexity in control plane.

Marta: quick q — how do you imagine signalization from runtime to control plane? lightweight counters or full tokenwise traces?

Kevin: lightweight counters + sampled token traces. counters: per-profile p50/p95 token-latency, quality-score histogram, fallback-counts. token traces only on canaries.

Sam: agree on counters. Also need a clear contract for when runtime must force fallback to a safer bitpath (no fuzzy heuristics). Suggest: absolute quality delta > 3% on evaluation set OR fallback-rate > X in last 5m.

Liz: can we make that configurable per-customer? enterprise customers will want tighter controls.

Kevin: yes — profile includes tolerances. runtime enforces hard minima (min_bit) and a fallback_order. Control plane owns policy and thresholds.

Marta: show the proposed profile schema?

Kevin: here is a minimal proposal (pseudo-JSON):

```json
{
  "profile_id": "hybrid-dyn-v1",
  "global": { "preferred_bits": [8,4], "min_bit": 4, "degradation_limit": 0.03 },
  "per_layer": {
    "attn.qkv": { "preferred_bits": [8,4], "min_bit": 4, "degradation_limit": 0.02 },
    "mlp.fc": { "preferred_bits": [4], "min_bit": 4, "degradation_limit": 0.05 }
  },
  "fallback_order": ["model_variant","per_layer","global"],
  "telemetry_tags": ["profile_id","slice","canary"]
}
```

Sam: nice. A couple of operational details:
- runtime should emit events when it uses a non-preferred bit (e.g., "used_bit=4 layer=attn.qkv profile=hybrid-dyn-v1").
- sample 0.1% of requests for tokenwise diff against golden (only on canary/opt-in).

runtime-bot: NOTE: runtime change required: expose a per-request bit-hint header and a telemetry endpoint for sampled diffs. (deployed->staging by CI)

ops-oncall: for rollbacks — we need a playbook entry. If fallback_count spikes > 5% in 2m and latency p95 increases > 30%, auto-disable profile and switch to pinned stable variant.

Marta: on quality scoring — propose using our existing QA eval harness but with smaller slices: short-FQA, long-context, instruction-following. We should attach degradation_limit per slice rather than global only.

Kevin: good point. update: add "slices" to schema and allow per-slice degradation_limit. Example: 

```json
"slices": {
  "short_fqa": { "degradation_limit": 0.02 },
  "long_ctx": { "degradation_limit": 0.04 }
}
```

Liz: any perf estimates? do we know cost of per-layer checking + sampled diffs on GPU runtime?

Sam: rough numbers from local tests (gpt-4-small mimic): enabling per-layer tracking + counters adds ~0.5% CPU and ~1–2% infra overhead overall. Sampled diffs (0.1%) negligible for latency but increases logging volume.

Kevin: actionable items:
- I will open RFC diff with the profile schema + policy examples.
- Marta: add per-slice evaluation integration to the QA harness.
- Sam: prototype telemetry events and a small canary job (1% traffic) with sampled diffs.
- Liz / Ops: draft rollback thresholds and playbook fragment.

Marta: ACK, will add test matrix to RFC.

Sam: ACK, will run perf sweep tomorrow.

Liz: ACK, will tag ops-oncall for playbook review.

Kevin: thanks all. If nobody objects I'll send the RFC link and schedule a 30m sync for next Tue to finalize guardrails. :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: +1 — include automatic disablement and alert routing to paging policy.

Kevin: filed: https://rfc.internal/4339-dyn-bit-negotiation (will attach experiments).
